newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-UNHERALDED TENERIFE BLAST FEYENOORD OUT OF UEFA CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UNHERALDED TENERIFE BLAST FEYENOORD OUT OF UEFA CUP.

text.p: Tenerife scored one of the major upsets of the season when they knocked former European champions Feyenoord out of the UEFA Cup on Tuesday with a 4-2 second leg away win in Rotterdam after the sides drew 0-0 in the Canary Islands two weeks ago.
Their victory stole the limelight away from Brondby's remarkable 5-0 away win over Karlsruhe in Germany which was equally unexpected following Karlsruhe's 3-1 win in Copenhagen in the first leg.

But Tenerife's victory over a Feyenoord side currently second in the Dutch league and playing well recently, was completely against the formbook and put Tenerife into the last eight of the UEFA Cup for the first time in their history.

Tenerife, who are based in the Canaries off the north coast of Africa and are one of the most isolated outposts of European soccer, have slipped to 13th in the Spanish league after a bright start to the season and were in low spirits after losing 2-1 at home to Rayo Vallecano on Saturday.

But they raced into a 4-0 lead to silence an astonished home crowd with goals from Felipe (5th), Juanele (45th and 60th) and Pablo Paz (74th). Feyenoord, European champions in 1970 and winners of this competition in 1974, replied with two late consolation goals from Argentine Pablo Sanchez and Henk Vos.

Brondby, the only Danish side ever to reach the last four of a European club competition -- they were in the semifinals of this competition in 1991 -- took another step towards reaching at least the same stage again.
They crushed Karlsruhe 5-0 after losing the home leg 3-1 having trailed 0-3 before a last-minute goal in Copenhagen gave them an outside chance in the second leg.

They took that chance with both hands, never looking back after Ruben Bagger, who scored in the last minute in the first leg, opened the scoring after 41 minutes. Dan Egger made it 3-3 on aggregate just before halftime and three more in the second half from Kim Vilfort and Peter Moeller (2) gave them victory.

It was a night to forget for the Germans as Hamburg crashed 2-0 at home to lose 5-0 on aggregate to Monaco. Hamburg's miserable night was completed when their Bosnian striker Hasan Salihamidzic was sent off in the last minute. Nigerian Victor Ikpeba (62nd) and Ali Bernabia (88th penalty) scored for the visitors.
Schalke restored some pride for the Bundesliga when they beat Club Brugge 2-1 to win 3-2 on aggregate and reach the last eight of a European competition for the first time in 23 years.
Newcastle United also reached the last eight of the UEFA Cup for the first time in almost 30 years when they beat Metz 2-0 at home.

Two late goals from Colombian Faustino Asprilla after 80 and 82 minutes gave the English side a 3-1 aggregate victory. His first was a close-ranger header, his second followed a rare show of individualism and Newcastle rode their luck after Metz dominated most of the play and wasted a string of scoring chances.

Another Englishman who enjoyed the night was Paul Ince who scored Inter Milan's second in their 2-0 win at Boavista where they sailed through to the quarter-finals 7-1 on aggregate. Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff opened the scoring with a 12th minute penalty.

The quarter-final line-up was completed by Anderlecht who beat Helsingborg 1-0 at home for a 1-0 aggregate win, and Valencia, who drew 2-2 in Turkey against Besiktas to go through 5-3. The draw for the quarter-finals, which will be played next March, will be made in Geneva next week.
